input_signals.name: Clean Accrual Net Capital Return
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ADD(prstkc, dvc), dltr), ADD(sstk, dltis)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with persistently clean accruals and net capital return will earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Low or negative accruals indicate earnings backed by cash flow, while repurchases, dividends, and debt retirement signal reduced dependence on external financing. The interaction favors firms whose financing actions are supported by accounting quality rather than by new capital raising.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ma( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 3 ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( add( add( prstkc, dvc ), dltr ), add( sstk, dltis ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual Financing Gap Strain
input_signals.expression: SUB(MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dltr), dvc)), at), RATIO(oancf, at)))), MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))), RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(prstkc, dltr), dvc)), at), RATIO(oancf, at))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High accrual earnings combined with a sign-sensitive external financing gap indicates weak internally funded quality and predicts lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids dividing by the absolute value of operating cash flow, preserving the distinction between cash-burning and cash-generating firms without creating near-zero denominator explosions. The financing leg measures net capital raised less capital returned, penalized further when operating cash flow is weak, so the interaction is broader than simple equity issuance.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( sub( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dltr ), dvc ) ), at ), ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) ), mul( rank( neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ), rank( neg( sub( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( prstkc, dltr ), dvc ) ), at ), ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EquityFunded Receivables Inventory Build
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms issuing net equity while receivables and inventories are consuming cash will earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual leg is sign-corrected so that high values represent receivable and inventory increases, not liquidation. Equity issuance during this operating build may indicate that reported growth is not converting into cash and is being supported by external shareholders.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( neg( add( recch, invch ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtAdjusted CurrentAccrual Issuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1))), ADD(DELTA(lct, 1), dp)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high debt-adjusted current accruals while raising net external capital will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This uses a balance-sheet accrual construction that explicitly adds back current debt changes, avoiding the mechanical short-debt versus working-capital conflict. The financing leg captures net external capital raising, so the signal targets firms whose noncash operating accrual buildup is being supported by outside capital rather than internal cash generation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( add( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), add( delta( dlc, 1 ), delta( txp, 1 ) ) ), add( delta( lct, 1 ), dp ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtFunded Payout CashShortfall
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(MIN(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at), SUB(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), RATIO(oancf, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High-accrual firms that borrow while payouts exceed internally generated operating cash flow will earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg is high only when net debt issuance and a payout-versus-cash-flow shortfall are both elevated, directly identifying the debt-funded payout mechanism. This avoids treating payouts as mechanically bearish; payouts become negative only when paired with weak cash conversion and external borrowing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( min( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ), sub( ratio( add( prstkc, dvc ), at ), ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WorkingCapitalBuild FinancingDeficit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with receivable and inventory buildup financed externally despite weak operating cash flow will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual leg uses the sign-corrected cash-flow-statement components, so high values capture cash-consuming working-capital accumulation. Pairing that buildup with an external-financing-minus-cash-flow gap focuses on operating growth that is not self-funded.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( neg( add( recch, invch ) ), at ) ), rank( sub( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtIssue EarningsShortfall AccrualStress
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(dltis, dltr), ib), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high accrual earnings that borrow more than their reported earnings will earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg avoids reusing operating cash flow and instead asks whether new debt financing exceeds accounting profits. When earnings already fail to convert into cash, debt issuance above reported income suggests that even stated profitability is insufficient to fund the firm’s needs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sub( dltis, dltr ), ib ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ReceivableTradeCredit FundingGap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(NEG(recch), apalch), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with receivable growth not offset by supplier trade credit and simultaneous net external financing will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: NEG(recch) captures cash-consuming receivable accumulation, while subtracting apalch adjusts for whether suppliers are funding that build through payables. A positive trade-credit gap paired with outside financing suggests customers are being financed by shareholders or creditors rather than by internally generated cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( neg( recch ), apalch ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: OtherAccrual ExternalFunding Drain
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(txach, aoloch)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with cash-consuming tax and other operating accrual changes while raising net external capital will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids reusing the prior debt-adjusted current-accrual formula and does not subtract earnings from the financing leg. The mechanism is that opaque non-working-capital accrual drains are more suspicious when the firm must simultaneously raise outside capital.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( neg( add( txach, aoloch ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitableAccrual EquityIssuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(ib, at))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms issuing net equity while reporting positive accrual-heavy earnings will earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual condition requires both a high earnings-minus-cash-flow gap and high reported income, so the signal is not driven by loss firms mechanically needing equity. Equity issuance is most suspect when management can sell shares against apparently strong but weakly cash-backed earnings.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( ib, at ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: PostFunding AccrualDeterioration
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), RANK(LAG(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose accrual quality deteriorates after prior external financing will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests a timing mechanism rather than another contemporaneous financing composite: outside capital was raised first, and cash conversion worsens afterward. If external financing funded low-quality growth or delayed recognition of operating weakness, subsequent accrual deterioration should be especially informative.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( lag( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: WorkingCapital DebtBeyondEarnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(dltis, dltr), ib), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with receivable and inventory buildup while net debt issuance exceeds reported earnings will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual leg uses the correct cash-flow-statement sign, so high values capture cash-consuming working-capital accumulation. Borrowing beyond reported income is especially concerning when operating assets are absorbing cash, suggesting growth is debt-funded rather than self-financing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( neg( add( recch, invch ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sub( dltis, dltr ), ib ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExternalFunding CashDrain AccrualStrain
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with accrual-heavy earnings that raise external capital without building cash reserves will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the dual-issuance MIN with a funding-use mechanism: external financing is more concerning when proceeds are absorbed rather than retained as cash. It avoids subtracting operating cash flow again from the financing leg, reducing overlap with prior cash-flow-deficit constructs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ), rank( sub( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), ratio( delta( che, 1 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WorkingCapitalBuild CashUseFunding
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with receivable and inventory buildup financed externally without a corresponding cash buildup will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual leg is sign-corrected so high values capture cash-consuming receivable and inventory accumulation. Pairing that operating build with external financing net of cash accumulation targets firms where outside capital appears to be absorbed by low-quality working-capital growth rather than retained liquidity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( neg( add( recch, invch ) ), at ) ), rank( sub( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), ratio( delta( che, 1 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PostFunding HighAccrualDeterioration
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))), RANK(LAG(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose accrual quality deteriorates into an already high-accrual state after prior external financing will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier timing signal may have had weak portfolio evidence because a pure change leg can select benign reversals or firms deteriorating from very clean starting points. This version requires the deterioration to leave the firm with high current accruals, producing a cleaner short portfolio of post-financing accounting stress rather than transitory accrual movement.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( rank( delta( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ), rank( lag( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: OtherAccrual CashUseFunding
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(txach, aoloch)), at)), RANK(SUB(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with opaque tax and other accrual cash drains while external financing is not retained as cash will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This shifts the accrual leg away from the heavily tested earnings-minus-cash-flow and receivable-inventory channels. Opaque accrual drains are more suspicious when outside capital is simultaneously being absorbed rather than building a liquidity buffer.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( neg( add( txach, aoloch ) ), at ) ), rank( sub( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), ratio( delta( che, 1 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dilution ReceivableAcceleration
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(NEG(recch), at))), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with accelerating receivable buildup and shareholder dilution will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the equity-plus-cash-drawdown MIN template with a revenue-quality mechanism: receivables accelerating faster than cash collections can indicate aggressive sales recognition. When that deterioration coincides with share-count growth, the firm may be using dilution to support reported growth that is not converting to cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( accel( ratio( neg( recch ), at ) ) ), rank( growth( csho, 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: ReceivableSkew ExternalFunding
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(NEG(recch), NEG(invch)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with receivable growth exceeding inventory growth while raising net external capital will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This drops the sparse payables adjustment and focuses on a higher-coverage receivable-skew accrual pattern. Receivables rising without a matching inventory build is more consistent with collection or revenue-recognition risk, and external financing suggests the firm is funding customers rather than generating cash internally.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( neg( recch ), neg( invch ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: OtherAccrual DebtBeyondEarnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(txach, aoloch)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(dltis, dltr), ib), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with opaque tax and other accrual cash drains that borrow more than reported earnings will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Tax and other accrual changes are less transparent than standard receivable or inventory accruals, so cash-consuming movements may be harder for investors to interpret. Net debt issuance above reported income suggests that even stated profitability is insufficient to fund the firm’s needs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( neg( add( txach, aoloch ) ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sub( dltis, dltr ), ib ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: AccrualFirst ExternalIssuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(LAG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that raise external capital after a prior period of accrual-heavy earnings will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the profitability gate and cash-use template with a timing mechanism: accrual-heavy reporting comes first, external financing follows. The story is that managers may exploit temporarily inflated reported performance to issue securities before the weak cash conversion is fully priced.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( lag( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: NonDepAccrual NoncashDiluter
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at)), RANK(SUB(RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high non-depreciation accruals and share-count growth not matched by cash equity proceeds will earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids another external-financing-minus-cash-change construction and instead focuses on dilution quality. If shares outstanding rise without corresponding cash issuance, dilution may reflect stock compensation or stock-financed transactions, which is more concerning when earnings quality is already weak.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( sub( ib, oancf ), dp ), at ) ), rank( sub( rank( winsor( growth( csho, 1 ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WorkingCapitalBuild EquityNotDelevered

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with receivable and inventory buildup that issue equity without meaningful debt reduction will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the prior positive long-corner design into a directly bearish financing-use test with a clearer bad tail. Equity issuance is less defensible when cash-consuming working-capital growth persists and proceeds do not appear to repair leverage through net debt retirement.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( neg( add( recch, invch ) ), at ) ), rank( sub( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: TaxPayable DebtIssuer Pressure

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms accruing rising tax obligations while issuing net debt will underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the stale lagged-accrual and debt-beyond-earnings splice with a specific balance-sheet pressure channel. Rising taxes payable can indicate deferred cash obligations, and net borrowing alongside that accrual buildup suggests the firm is financing obligations that reported earnings have not converted into cash.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( delta( txp, 1 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ) )
